checks.result: passed; 8 tests, 0 failures, including a native FSEvents write smoke trace

acceptance_evidence.reference: A deterministic temporary-filesystem test writes allocated data inside and outside a watched root: the inside write becomes inferred detailed evidence while the outside allocation becomes an unknown-confidence unexplained cause. Monitoring policy tests prove watched, dynamically registered, active investigation, expired investigation, and excluded roots. Scanner tests prove metadata-only bounded enumeration plus unavailable-root and entry-limit disclosure. Synthetic FSEvents flags prove gap disclosure and exclusion filtering, while a live macOS FSEvents smoke test writes a file and receives a rescan-required path hint. Coalescing tests bound repeated matching writes, and explanation tests preserve limitations and weaken confidence across event gaps.

discovered_risks: FSEvents is intentionally notification-only and cannot establish creator-process identity; metadata rescans derive byte deltas with inferred confidence.
Whole-volume allocation can change outside configured roots, so residual growth is exported as unexplained rather than attributed speculatively.
FSEvents drop, wrap, mount, unmount, and root-change flags force unknown confidence and an explicit rescan limitation.
External volumes are sampled for aggregate capacity only when returned by the existing volume service; file-level monitoring remains limited to configured roots.
